text:
COP rose 2.4% today to close at $140.90, extending a strong two-week rally (up 12% since October 6th). The move follows news that the IEA warned of a severe diesel squeeze extending into 2027 due to Iran war disruptions and falling inventories, which sent oil prices higher — world oil is trading at $125.44 per barrel, well above the U.S. benchmark of $96.24. For a major oil producer and refiner like ConocoPhillips, sustained tight diesel markets and elevated global crude prices directly support both production revenue and refining margins.

The stock's momentum reflects a broader shift in energy market expectations: geopolitical disruption in the Middle East and supply tightness are now seen as structural, not temporary, which favors integrated energy companies positioned to benefit from higher prices and constrained supply over the coming year.
